bug_semantics: Rendering a ScriptObject recursively stringifies each member value without cycle detection. A ScriptObject whose member points back to itself therefore repeatedly re-enters the object-to-string path; with ObjectRecursionLimit left at its default value of 0, the guard is disabled and recursion continues until an uncatchable StackOverflowException terminates the host process.
flaw_origin: Commit cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e made ScriptObject rendering traverse the real stored member values and recursively call ScriptValueConverter.ToString on each one. Its parent exposed the InternalValue wrapper instead and had no dedicated recursive ScriptObject rendering block, so the advisory's self-referential ScriptObject path begins in this commit. Commit a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d later added an opt-in ObjectRecursionLimit guard but initialized it to 0 (unlimited), preserving the flaw by default rather than introducing the recursive attack path.
ai_marker: absent: the raw commit object for cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e has human author and committer Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com> and the message 'Fix pretty print object ScriptObject and ScriptArray, dump objects with {...} and [...]'; it contains no trailers, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other commit-object AI marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-grr9-747v-xvcp documents the {{ a }} self-referential ScriptObject PoC, explains that default ObjectRecursionLimit=0 disables the bound, and names 6.6.0 as patched. Its repository advisory API records vulnerable_version_range '6.5.8' and patched_versions '6.6.0'; the syndicated GHSA-PPRH-WGQR-2MMX/CVE-2026-74794 bundle summarizes the range as before 6.6.0.

git show cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e shows src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs adding a ScriptObject branch whose loop calls ToString(span, keyPair.Value), while src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptObject.cs changes GetEnumerator from item.Value (the InternalValue wrapper) to item.Value.Value (the attacker-controlled stored object). Together these are the smallest changes that make a self-reference flow back into the same renderer.

Direct parent-tree comparison git diff 790f00752e7b7392f2849452f37345852f313634 cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e -- src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptObject.cs proves both vulnerable changes are absent from the immediate parent: there is no dedicated recursive ScriptObject block and enumeration does not expose the stored member value.

git log -S ObjectRecursionLimit and git show a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d show the later guard checks ObjectRecursionLimit != 0 before enforcing depth, while TemplateContext initializes ObjectRecursionLimit=0 and documents 0 as unlimited. That mitigation first appears in 3.7.0 and therefore does not displace cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e as the BIC for recursive ScriptObject rendering.

git show a6fe6074199e5c04f4d29dc8d8e652b24d33e3e4 changes src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs from ObjectRecursionLimit=0 to ObjectRecursionLimit=20 and updates the documented default. This activates the existing depth check so a cycle raises a bounded exception instead of exhausting the process stack.

Version-tree checks resolve 6.5.8 to b640147b792c41aa3756b463673c741e46c44470 and 6.6.0 to b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7. git diff 6.5.8^{commit} 6.6.0^{commit} -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs shows the default boundary 0 to 20; git tag --contains a6fe6074199e5c04f4d29dc8d8e652b24d33e3e4 includes 6.6.0 but not 6.5.8. git describe --contains places the BIC before v0.1.0, consistent with the repository history showing the vulnerable rendering path predates the patched boundary.

git cat-file commit cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e provides the only AI-attribution evidence used: one parent, author/committer Alexandre Mutel, and no trailers or bot/AI marker. Commit URL: https://github.com/scriban/scriban/commit/cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e; direct fix URL: https://github.com/scriban/scriban/commit/a6fe6074199e5c04f4d29dc8d8e652b24d33e3e4.
reasoning: The advisory's concrete attack is not merely that a configurable limit later had an unsafe default; it is that rendering a circular ScriptObject follows member values back into the same formatter. History reconstruction isolates cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e: it both exposes actual ScriptObject member values during enumeration and adds recursive per-member stringification. The immediate parent lacks those operations, so the demonstrated self-reference cannot take this recursive path there. The 2021 a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d commit recognized the danger and added a depth guard, but its explicit zero default leaves that guard inactive and does not originate the earlier attack path. The direct 2026 fix a6fe6074199e5c04f4d29dc8d8e652b24d33e3e4 changes the default to 20; it is absent from 6.5.8 and contained in the 6.6.0 release tree. Finally, the BIC is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a squash or move, and its raw commit object has no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
